maria (security): Heads up — our nightly backup job for pg-replicas wrote a snapshot to s3://redwood-qa-backups/2026-03-21/ that appears to be missing SSE-CMEK metadata. I ran a quick head and saw no x-amz-server-side-encryption headers.

sam (eng-infra): Oof. Which job? backup-uploader-v2?

maria (security): backup-uploader-v2. It normally goes through the uploader service account which should have a kms:Encrypt grant. Looks like a recent RBAC change touched that SA last night.

jordan (encops): Can you paste the head-object output?

maria (security): Sure:

```
$ aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-qa-backups --key 2026-03-21/pg-replica-2026-03-21.tar.gz
{
  "ContentLength": 345678901,
  "ContentType": "application/gzip",
  "Metadata": {},
  "ETag": "\"abc123\""
}
```

lee (sre): No SSE headers in that output. Do we have object-lock/versioning that would indicate an older encrypted copy?

sam (eng-infra): Bucket has default encryption set, but uploader can override if its client doesn't request SSE. I want to check uploader logs for a fallback error.

maria (security): I grepped logs and found this error around 00:12 UTC: `kms:AccessDenied` when trying to generate a data key. Then the uploader continued and uploaded the file without encryption.

jordan (encops): That's the key. The RBAC change likely removed the `kms:GenerateDataKey` grant from the uploader SA. If the client code catches the error and proceeds, it can write unencrypted objects. We need to confirm scope and whether any customer PII was in that snapshot.

kai (product): That QA snapshot may contain redacted customer copies; prob ok, but we need to treat as sensitive until proven otherwise.

lee (sre): Quick checklist: (1) identify all objects uploaded during the window (00:00–01:00 UTC), (2) snapshot object metadata for audit, (3) block further uploads until fixed, (4) rotate any exposed keys if needed.

maria (security): I'm running a query to enumerate uploads from uploader-v2 in that hour. Results so far: 6 objects, all without SSE headers.

jordan (encops): Run `encops-verify` on those objects (we have a tool that checks encryption headers + KMS grants). If it flags unencrypted objects, move them to quarantine prefix and set ACL to private. Also collect ETag and upload timestamps.

sam (eng-infra): On it. Command I'm running: `./tools/encops-verify --bucket redwood-qa-backups --prefix 2026-03-21/ --since 2026-03-21T00:00Z --until 2026-03-21T01:00Z --quarantine-prefix quarantine/`

kms-bot: detected IAM change: role uploader-service-sa removed policy grant kms:GenerateDataKey at 2026-03-21T00:05:12Z by deploy-bot. Refer to audit id: AID-20260321-4421.

sam (eng-infra): Ah the deploy-bot rollback. That explains it — a prior PR removed a permissive grant and deploy-bot rolled a hotfix that overapplied a strict policy.

maria (security): Action items I propose:
- quarantine the unencrypted objects (jordan)
- restore kms:GenerateDataKey to uploader SA with least-privileges (sam)
- audit the uploader to fail uploads when encryption fails (jordan + sam)
- run a data-scope scan to confirm PII not present (maria + kai)
- create incident ticket INC-2026-042 and notify compliance (maria)

jordan (encops): I'll quarantine now and attach a csv with object keys + ETags. Also adding a canary that prevents silent fallback: change client to `abort_on_kms_error=true`.

sam (eng-infra): I'll open a PR to restore the minimal grant and add a test to the deploy pipeline to catch this RBAC regression. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/5423

lee (sre): We should also add an alert: if uploader encounters `kms:AccessDenied` more than 3 times in 10m, page eng-security.

maria (security): Agreed. Also capturing timeline for postmortem: 00:05 policy change -> 00:12 uploader error -> 00:13 fallback upload -> 00:20 detection by maria.

kai (product): Do we need to notify QA customers? We should get legal/PR eyes before sending anything external.

maria (security): I'll file INC-2026-042 and ping legal + compliance. For now label this as internal incident and treat objects as sensitive.

jordan (encops): Quarantine done. CSV uploaded to `s3://redwood-ops-quarantine/INC-2026-042/objects.csv`. Permissions locked.

sam (eng-infra): Rollback policy patched in staging, tests added. I'll push to prod after a short verification window (15m).

maria (security): Thanks. After prod deploy, sam + jordan, re-run `encops-verify` across the entire backup prefix for the past 48h to ensure no other silent fallbacks.

lee (sre): Adding monitoring ticket MON-2026-101 to create alarm on missing SSE headers for newly created objects in backup buckets.

maria (security): Final note: make sure audit logs include the deploy-bot actor and policy diff in the incident artifacts. That audit id from kms-bot (AID-20260321-4421) should be attached to the ticket.

sam (eng-infra): Acknowledge. I'll comment on INC-2026-042 with the PR link and audit logs.

maria (security): Great. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

lee (sre): :shipit:

kms-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 created by maria (security) at 2026-03-21T02:03:40Z.
